blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.
blocks.zh: 基因视觉核查器在推进多式智能方面发挥着关键作用。 为了在涉及组成要求的复杂多式情景中加强视觉核查员的稳健性,我们超越了仅产生True/False离散判断的常规二进制核查员,并引入了自动将复杂提示或环境规则分解为精细分量的核查员,并按点定分,以提供连续和更加翔实的批评信号。 我们的实验进一步表明,这些结构化和可解释的产出改进了核查者对域外多式联运评论任务的概括。 为了培训这一核查员,我们采用了脱钩的RL培训战略,联合优化子问题层面的二进制判断和全球对等评分,利用准确的当地反馈来发展精细的核查能力,为全球一级可靠的连续评分奠定基础。 在一般的强化学习框架内,我们首先以经验证明,在传统的文本到图像的假设中,拟议的分级核查器大大超过二进制核查器。 然后,我们把调查扩大到统治基因世界的模型,根据明确的规则,利用基因模型进行世界模拟和世界推理。 从理论角度看,我们进一步表明,双向核查范式产生的评论比地面真实图像出现时的直指表述更准确,在马兹和数都等各种结构化的世界模型任务上的经验结果进一步证实了我们的方法的有效性。 总而言之,我们的调查结果提出了一个关键的见解:从基因模型向结构化的世界模型化剂的过渡,关键取决于能否获得准确的对等分级视觉核查器。

blocks.en: 1  Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Multimodal generative models have made remarkable progress in recent years ( Cao et al., 2025 ; Seedream et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ) , producing visually compelling images conditioned on textual descriptions. Beyond visual fidelity ( Wiedemer et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2024b ; Yang et al., 2025b ) , a central challenge lies in whether generated images faithfully follow complex instructions and reflect coherent world knowledge ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Jin et al., 2026 ; Deng et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025a ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) . Motivated by this challenge, visual verifiers have emerged as a crucial component for assessing the correctness of generated results. By providing feedback on the alignment between images and textual descriptions, verifiers not only serve as evaluation tools, but also act as general critic models for inference-time scaling and reinforcement learning-based training. As generative models are increasingly applied to open-ended environments and reasoning-intensive tasks, the reliability and expressiveness of visual verifiers become a key bottleneck for advancing multimodal intelligence.
blocks.zh: 近年来,多式联运基因模型取得了显著进展(Cao等人,2025年;Seedream等人,2025年;Chen等人,2026年)。 超越视觉忠诚(Wiedemer等,2025;Zhang等,2024b;Yang等,2025b),一个中心挑战在于所生成的图像是否忠实地遵循复杂的指示并反映一致的世界知识(周等,2025;Jin等,2026;邓等,2025;杨等,2025a;黄等,2026;张等,2026b.). 受这一挑战的驱使,视觉核查员已成为评估所产生结果正确性的一个关键组成部分。 通过提供图像与文字描述相匹配的反馈,核查者不仅作为评价工具,还充当推论时间缩放和强化以学习为基础的培训的一般评论模型. 随着基因模型越来越多地被应用于开放式环境和推理密集型任务,视觉验证器的可靠性和表达性成为推进多模式智能的关键瓶颈.

blocks.en:
Despite their importance, most existing visual verifiers ( Zhang et al., 2025b ; Wang et al., 2025a ; Xiong et al., 2025 ) adopt a binary judgment paradigm that produces only True/False decisions about whether an image satisfies a given prompt. Although simple and efficient, this design has several inherent limitations.
First, binary supervision provides coarse feedback that fails to capture the partial correctness of generated samples. By assigning the same negative label to imperfect samples of varying quality, binary rewards obscure meaningful quality differences and weaken the within-group learning signals required by group-relative reinforcement learning.
Moreover, the limited information conveyed by binary labels may encourage shortcut learning and increase susceptibility to reward hacking ( Shao et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026c ) , as models may exploit superficial patterns to predict the expected labels without adequately reasoning about the e subtl compositional relationships among objects, attributes, and spatial constraints.
blocks.zh:
尽管它们很重要,但大多数现有的视觉验证器 (Zhang等,2025b;Wang等,2025a;Xiong等,2025)采用二进制判断范式,只产生True/False关于一幅图像是否满足给定提示的决定. 这种设计虽然简单而高效,但有一些固有的局限性.
第一,二进制监理提供粗糙的反馈,无法捕捉所生成样品的部分正确性. 通过给质量各异的不完善样本打上同样的负面标签,二进制奖励模糊了有意义的质量差异并削弱了群相相强化学习所需的群内学习信号.
此外,二进制标签传递的有限信息可能鼓励捷径学习并增加奖励黑客的易感性(Shao等,2025;Wang等,2026c),因为模型可能利用表面模式来预测预期的标签,而没有充分推理物体、属性和空间限制之间的电子下层组成关系。

blocks.en: To address these limitations, we propose the Decomposed Graded Verifier (OmniVerifier-C1) , which automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained sub-questions and performs structured reasoning over each component. It assigns continuous scores based on the proportion of satisfied sub-questions, capturing partial correctness and providing informative critique signals. Our experiments demonstrate that decomposition-based structured reasoning significantly improves the verifier’s out-of-domain multimodal critic capabilities. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise 0/1 feedback on individual sub-questions to develop strong fine-grained verification capabilities that support reliable global scoring. Moreover, our theoretical analysis shows that the decomposition-and-scoring paradigm better preserves the underlying true quality ordering among generated samples, providing finer-grained learning signals for group-relative reinforcement learning.
blocks.zh: 为了解决这些局限性,我们提议采用分解的分级验证器(OmniVerifer-C1),它将复杂的提示或环境规则自动分解成细微的分问题,并对每个部分进行结构化的推理。 它根据满意子问题的比例分配连续的分数,捕捉到部分正确性并提供信息性的批评信号. 我们的实验表明,以分解为基础的结构化推理大大地改善了核查员在域外的多式联运评论能力。 为了培训这一核查员,我们采用了脱钩的RL培训战略,联合优化子问题层面的二进制判断和全球对等评分,利用对单个子问题的精确0/1反馈,以发展强大的精细的验证能力,支持可靠的全球评分. 此外,我们的理论分析表明,分解和评分范式更好地维护了生成样本中的基础性真正质量顺序,为群体相对强化学习提供了更精细的学习信号。

blocks.en: Building upon this verifier, we further explore its role as a generative reward model for reinforcement learning across two types of tasks. First, we apply the verifier to traditional text-to-image alignment, where it provides fine-grained feedback that encourages generative models to satisfy detailed compositional relationship. Second, we extend our study to the more reasoning-intensive and challenging setting of structured generative world modeling , where generative models are used to simulate environments and reason over sequential states. In these rule-governed environments, we find that pairwise verification, which compares generated states against ground-truth states, provides more accurate and reliable critiques than pointwise verification. This observation suggests that the effectiveness of visual verification in rule-governed world-modeling scenarios critically depends on the availability of reference states for comparison. Extensive experiments across diverse tasks, such as Maze and Sudoku, demonstrate that the proposed verifier provides more reliable reward signals and substantially improves reinforcement learning performance.
blocks.zh: 在这个核查人的基础上,我们进一步探讨其作为在两类任务中加强学习的基因奖励模式的作用。 首先,我们把验证器应用于传统的文本到图像的对齐,它提供了精细的反馈,鼓励基因模型满足详细的组成关系. 第二,我们的研究扩展到结构化基因世界模型的更加推理密集和具有挑战性的设定,其中基因模型用于模拟环境和理性,而不是相继状态。 在这些规则管理的环境中,我们发现,将生成的国家与地面真实国家进行比较的双向核查,提供了比指针核查更准确和可靠的批评。 这一看法表明,在规则管理的世界模型情景中,视觉核查的有效性主要取决于可供比较的参考状态。 跨不同任务的广泛实验,如"Maze"和"sudoku",表明所拟议的验证器提供了更可靠的奖励信号并大大地改进了强化的学习性能.

blocks.en: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: • We propose the Decomposed Graded Verifier , which automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained sub-questions, performs structured reasoning over each component, and assigns continuous scores based on the proportion of satisfied sub-questions. Our experiments demonstrate that its structured outputs significantly improve out-of-domain multimodal critic capabilities. • We introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise 0/1 feedback on individual sub-questions to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable scoring. • We demonstrate that the proposed verifier serves as an effective generative reward model for reinforcement learning, improving performance in both traditional text-to-image generation and rule-governed generative world modeling tasks. • We provide empirical validation across diverse structured reasoning environments, showing that accurate pairwise decomposed verifiers are a key enabler for transforming generative models into rule-governed world-modeling agents.
blocks.zh: • 我们的贡献可归纳如下: 我们建议分解分级验证器,它自动将复杂的提示或环境规则分解为细微分级问题,对每个组成部分进行结构化推理,并根据满意分级问题的比例分配连续分数. 我们的实验表明,其结构化产出大大提高了域外多式联运评论能力。 我们采用脱钩的RL培训战略,联合优化子问题层面的二进制判断和全球对等评分,利用对单个子问题的精确0/1反馈来发展精细的认证能力,为可靠的评分提供基础. 我们表明,拟议的核查者是加强学习的有效基因奖励模式,提高了传统文字到图像生成和规则管理基因世界建模任务的绩效。 我们提供不同结构推理环境的经验性验证,表明精确的双相分解验证器是将基因模型转化为规则治理的世界模型剂的关键使能器.

blocks.en: 2  Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Generative Verifier or Reward Models
blocks.zh: 2.1 基因验证或奖励模式

blocks.en:
Generative reward models ( Mahan et al., 2024 ; Malik et al., 2025 ; Tan et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2026c ) differ fundamentally from traditional reward models ( Xu et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2024a ; Ouyang et al., 2022 ; Zhang et al., 2024c ) in that they produce explicit rationales rather than merely assigning scalar scores. OmniVerifier ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) first introduces the concept of Generative Universal Verifier and presents ViVerBench, a comprehensive and challenging benchmark for evaluating multimodal reasoning and critique capabilities.
DeepSeekMath-V2 ( Shao et al., 2025 ) further proposes meta-verification and integrates it into verifier training to enhance faithfulness and reliability.
OmniVerifier-M1 ( Zhang et al., 2026d ) extends meta-verification to multimodal scenarios by introducing symbolic spatial annotations, such as bounding boxes, points or lines as verifiable rationales. These rule-based supervision signals substantially alleviate reward hacking and enhance verifier generalization.
Despite their improved interpretability, existing generative verifiers still rely on coarse binary decisions as final judgments, and thus struggle to provide dense and optimization-friendly reward signals for reinforcement learning.
In this paper, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy to train the Decomposed Graded Verifier, which provides reliable continuous scores through explicit fine-grained decomposition.
blocks.zh:
基因奖励模式(Mahan等,2024;Malik等,2025;Tan等,2024;Liu等,2024;Wang等,2026c)与传统奖励模式(徐等,2023;张等,2024a; Ouyang等,2022;Zhang等,2024c),因为它们提出了明确的理由,而不仅仅是分配分数。 OmniVerifer(Zhang等人,2025年b)首先提出了Generative Universal Verifer的概念,并提出了ViVer Bench,这是评价多式联运推理和批评能力的全面而有挑战性的基准。
DeepSeekMath-V2(Shao等人,2025年)进一步提出元验证,并将其纳入验证员培训,以提高忠诚度和可靠性.
OmniVerifer-M1 (Zhang等, 2026d) 将元验证扩展至多模式情景,引入了象征性的空间说明,例如将边框,点或线作为可核查的理由. 这些基于规则的监管信号大大地缓解了奖励黑客化,并增强了验证器的通俗化.
尽管其可解释性得到改进,但现有的基因验证员仍然依靠粗糙的二进制决定作为最终判断,因此努力为强化学习提供密集和最优化的奖励信号.
在本文中,我们引入了脱钩的RL训练策略来训练脱钩的分级验证器,通过明确的精细分解提供可靠的连续分数.

blocks.en: 2.2 Generative Model as World Reasoner
blocks.zh: 2.2 基因模型作为世界理性

blocks.en:
Multimodal generative models have made remarkable progress ( Lin et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2026a ; Zhang et al., 2026c ) in semantic alignment and aesthetic quality. Beyond visual fidelity, they are increasingly expected to serve as reasoning-capable world simulators ( OpenAI, 2025b ; Google, 2025 ; Google, 2024 ) .
To quantify the world reasoning capabilities of current generative models, several benchmarks ( Li et al., 2025 ; Sun et al., 2025 ; Han et al., 2026 ) have been proposed. WISE ( Niu et al., 2025 ) focuses on evaluating generative models’ understanding of cultural commonsense and scientific knowledge.
MMGR ( Cai et al., 2025 ) is designed to probe generative models’ spatial, temporal, physical, and logical reasoning capabilities.
Motivated by these challenges, recent studies ( Tan et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) have explored new training paradigms and input modalities to learn the underlying dynamics of world evolution.
Emu3.5 ( Cui et al., 2025 ) advances world modeling by learning native next-state prediction over long-horizon interleaved vision-language sequences.
UnityVideo ( Huang et al., 2025 ) improves world-aware video generation through unified multi-modal and multi-task learning across diverse visual representations.
In contrast to these efforts, we focus on improving the reliability and accuracy of reinforcement learning rewards for visual generation in rule-governed world-modeling scenarios, thereby encouraging generative models to develop stronger and more generalizable world reasoning capabilities.

blocks.en: 3  OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier
blocks.zh: 3 Omni验证器- C1: 分解分级验证器

blocks.en: In this section, we first analyze the theoretical advantages of the graded verifier over the binary verifier as a generative reward model. We then empirically demonstrate that our verifier develops fine-grained and generalizable multimodal verification capabilities through the Decoupled RL strategy, which jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们首先分析分级验证器相对于二进制验证器的理论优势,作为基因奖励模型. 然后,我们通过经验证明,我们的核查者通过脱钩的RL战略发展精细和可通用的多式核查能力,该战略共同优化了子问题层面的二进制判断和全球对等评分。

blocks.en: 3.1 Theoretical Advantage of Decomposed Graded Rewards for Generative RL
blocks.zh: 3.1 Generative RL分级奖励理论优势

blocks.en: Figure 2: Overview of our training pipeline. Stage 1 trains the Decomposed Graded Verifier with decoupled reinforcement learning to produce fine-grained continuous rewards. Stage 2 introduces a pairwise judgment paradigm that provides cleaner and more reliable reward signals for generative model reinforcement learning.
blocks.zh: 图 2:我们培训管道概况. 第一阶段培训分解分级验证员,进行分解分级强化学习,以产生精细分级的连续奖励. 第二阶段引入了双向判断范式,为基因模型强化学习提供更清洁更可靠的奖励信号.

blocks.en:
Binary verifiers have emerged as an effective tool for improving text-to-image generation quality through inference-time scaling ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) .
When they detect semantic inconsistencies between a generated image and its textual description, they produce editing instructions that guide the generative model to iteratively refine the visual output.
For this purpose, coarse binary feedback is often sufficient, as the verifier primarily serves as a gating mechanism that determines whether further refinement is needed.
However, binary verifiers face inherent limitations when used as reward models for reinforcement learning, as their feedback is insufficiently dense and discriminative to distinguish among imperfect samples of varying visual quality and thereby guide effective generative policy optimization.
blocks.zh:
二进制验证器已成为通过推论时间缩放提高文本到图像生成质量的有效工具(张等,2025b.).
当它们检测出生成的图像与其文字描述之间的语义不一致时,它们会生成编辑指令来引导基因模型迭代地完善视觉输出.
为此,粗重的二进制反馈往往已经足够了,因为核查者主要充当了判断是否需要作进一步改进的取景机制.
然而,二进制验证器在用作强化学习的奖励模型时面临固有的局限性,因为他们的反馈不够密集和有区别,无法区分不同视觉质量的不完善样本,从而指导有效的基因政策优化.

blocks.en: To address this limitation, we introduce the Decomposed Graded Verifier, a structured verification paradigm that elicits continuous scores from visual verifiers. Instead of reducing assessment to a single binary judgment, it decomposes a complex prompt into fine-grained sub-questions, evaluates each sub-question individually with binary judgments, and aggregates these local decisions into a continuous score that reflects the degree of prompt satisfaction. By preserving partial correctness in generated samples, this fine-grained reward signal provides denser and more optimization-friendly supervision for reinforcement learning.

blocks.en: 3.2 Graded Verification Enhances Multimodal Reasoning and Critique Capabilities
blocks.zh: 3.2 分级核查加强了多式联运的理由和关键能力

blocks.en: Binary verifiers supervise model training solely through the final True/False outcome, implicitly assuming that a correct verdict reflects a correct reasoning process. This assumption is often reasonable in domains such as mathematical problem solving, where the solution space is large and arriving at the correct answer typically requires coherent multi-step reasoning. However, it becomes much more fragile in binary multimodal critique tasks. Without explicit supervision over the judgment process, a verifier may exploit shallow visual patterns or shortcut cues to produce seemingly correct verdicts without genuinely understanding the underlying multimodal reasoning process ( Wang et al., 2026c ; Shao et al., 2025 ) , thereby leading to reward hacking
blocks.zh: 二进制验证员只通过最终的"真"/"假"结果来监督模型训练,隐含地假设正确的判断反映了正确的推理过程. 这种假设在数学问题解决等领域往往是合理的,在这样的领域,解决方案空间很大,得出正确的答案通常需要连贯的多步骤推理. 然而,在二进制多式联运批评任务中,它变得更加脆弱。 如果不对判断过程进行明确的监督,核查人可能利用浅浅的视觉模式或捷径提示来作出看似正确的判断,而不真正了解基本的多式联运推理过程(Wang等,2026c; Shao等人,2025年),从而导致奖励黑客.

As shown in Fig. 2 , given a textual prompt c c and its corresponding generated image y y , we convert each pair into K + 1 K+1 reinforcement learning samples, where K K denotes the number of decomposed sub-questions. Specifically, one sample is used for decomposition-based continuous scoring policy optimization, while the remaining K K samples are used for binary fine-grained judgment policy optimization.
For the decomposition-based scoring sample, the verifier takes the textual prompt c c and the generated image y y as input, and is trained to predict the global alignment score induced by the decomposition. Given the predicted score S ^ ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \hat{S}\in[0,1] and the ground-truth score S ∗ ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] S^{*}\in[0,1] , the reward is defined as ℛ score = 1 − | S ^ − S ∗ | \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{score}}=1-|\hat{S}-S^{*}| . For each fine-grained judgment sample, the verifier takes the k k -th sub-question Q k Q_{k} and the generated image y y as input, and is trained to predict the binary answer associated with this sub-question. Given the predicted answer A ^ k ∈ { 0 , 1 } \hat{A}_{k}\in\{0,1\} and the ground-truth answer A k ∗ ∈ { 0 , 1 } A_{k}^{*}\in\{0,1\} , the reward is defined as ℛ judgment = 𝟙 [ A ^ k = A k ∗ ] \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{judgment}}=\mathbbm{1}[\hat{A}_{k}=A_{k}^{*}] .
During reinforcement learning, we mix these two types of samples and optimize them with their respective rewards, forming a decoupled RL training scheme that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring. Precise 0/1 feedback on individual sub-questions enables the verifier to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring.

blocks.en:
Table 1 shows that the Decomposed Graded Verifier achieves stronger generalization than the Discrete Binary Verifier on ViVerBench, a comprehensive and challenging benchmark for evaluating multimodal reasoning and critique.
Notably, the Decomposed Graded Verifier requires supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the structured decomposition paradigm. By contrast, the Discrete Binary Verifier only needs to produce a binary True/False verdict with a corresponding textual explanation, and can therefore be directly optimized through reinforcement learning.
For a fair comparison, we evaluate the Discrete Binary Verifier in both RL-only and SFT+RL settings. The results show that the Discrete Binary Verifier consistently underperforms the Decomposed Graded Verifier, regardless of whether it is first adapted with SFT.
This indicates that the key factor is not the training pipeline itself, but the nature of the supervision signal. Binary supervision is highly compressed and sparse, which encourages the model to rely on shallow patterns rather than capturing complex semantic structures. In contrast, the Decomposed Graded Verifier decomposes complex tasks into multiple sub-questions and performs fine-grained judgments, thereby explicitly enforcing a structured reasoning process. This mechanism provides richer and more informative feedback signals, effectively mitigating reward hacking and substantially improving the model’s multimodal reasoning and critique capabilities.
Moreover, our Decoupled RL training strategy jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise 0/1 feedback on individual sub-questions to strengthen fine-grained verification capabilities and thereby provide a foundation for robust generalization to out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios.

blocks.en: Traditional text-to-image generation primarily targets semantic alignment, where a prompt may admit multiple diverse and visually plausible outputs, leaving no well-defined unique ground-truth image. By contrast, world simulation and reasoning tasks are rule-governed and highly structured, where the desired final state is often uniquely determined by the initial state and the underlying rules, thereby making a ground-truth image available in many scenarios. Motivated by this property, we explicitly introduce the ground-truth image as an additional visual input to the verifier, which simplifies the verification process and enables the verifier to produce more accurate and reliable reward signals for rule-governed generative world modeling.
blocks.zh: 传统的文字到图像生成主要针对语义上的对齐,即一个提示可能承认多种多样和视觉上可信的输出,从而留下没有明确界定的独特地面真实图像。 相形之下,世界模拟和推理任务都是由规则支配和高度结构化的,其中所期望的最终状态往往由初始状态和基础规则独有地决定,从而在许多情景中提供地真相图像. 以这种特性为动力,我们明确提出地面真实图像作为核查者的额外视觉输入,简化了核查过程,使核查者能够为统治下的基因世界模型制作更准确和可靠的奖励信号。

This property is crucial for post-training generative models, where the effectiveness of reinforcement learning hinges on the accuracy and stability of the reward signal.

blocks.en: The pairwise-trained model exhibits steadier and more pronounced performance improvements, whereas the pointwise-trained model shows clear performance fluctuations. Pointwise rewards require the verifier to infer an implicit target state, which can introduce substantial noise into the feedback in complex reasoning scenarios. In contrast, pairwise verification directly compares the generated result with the ground-truth image, reducing reliance on target-state inference and enabling reward signals to better reflect the true visual quality. This provides more reliable supervision for policy optimization and highlights the value of pairwise verification for developing generative models into rule-governed world-modeling agents.

Tables 3 and 4 show that SFT yields substantial performance gains, which can be primarily attributed to task-domain adaptation.
Since Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 has not been specifically trained on game-based image-to-image generation tasks, it often fails to interpret the required transformation. In practice, the model tends to either the model tends to either leave the input image unchanged or distort its original structure, indicating that it lacks the task-specific action priors required for this domain.
After supervised fine-tuning on our constructed game-based dataset, the generative model learns the visual style of these tasks and the corresponding rule-based transformation patterns. Although the model still often fails to produce fully correct solutions, it begins to perform meaningful operations toward the desired final state rather than generating irrelevant or destructive visual outputs, leading to clear performance improvements. These results indicate that SFT primarily equips the model with domain-specific execution ability , while subsequent reinforcement learning further endows the generative model with reasoning intelligence.

在监督我们构建的基于游戏的数据集进行微调后,基因模型学习了这些任务的视觉风格和相应的基于规则的转换模式. 尽管该模型仍然往往未能产生完全正确的解决方案,但它开始朝着理想的最终状态进行有意义的操作,而不是产生无关紧要或破坏性的视觉输出,从而导致明显的性能改进. 这些结果表明,SFT主要为模型配备了特定域的执行能力,而随后的强化学习进一步将基因模型赋予了推理智能.

blocks.en: In both multimodal understanding and generation models, the text encoder is often regarded as the primary source of reasoning intelligence. For generative models, this view implies that the text encoder interprets instructions and provides semantic guidance, while the DiT primarily executes the visual generation process. However, in our training pipeline, the text encoder remains frozen throughout both SFT and RL, and only the DiT parameters are updated. The reasoning capabilities observed after training suggest that reasoning intelligence is not encoded exclusively in the text encoder, as the DiT can also learn, internalize, and express capabilities for structured reasoning and rule-governed world modeling.
blocks.zh: 在多式联运理解和生成模型中,文本编码器常被视作推理智能的主要来源. 对于基因模型,这种观点意味着文本编码器解释指令并提供语义指导,而DiT主要执行视觉生成过程. 然而,在我们的培训过程中,文本编码器在整个SFT和RL中仍然被冻结,只有DiT参数被更新. 训练后观察到的推理能力表明推理智能并非完全在文本编码器中编码,因为DiT还可以学习,内化,并表达结构推理和规则治理的世界建模能力.

blocks.en: 6  Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: This work introduces the Decomposed Graded Verifier as an effective reward model for improving visual generation in both traditional text-to-image tasks and structured world-modeling scenarios. Our contributions are twofold. First, we propose a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that support accurate continuous scoring. Empirical results further demonstrate improved out-of-domain multimodal critic capabilities. Second, focusing on rule-governed world modeling, we introduce a pairwise verification paradigm that explicitly incorporates ground-truth images as visual references. This simplifies verification by shifting from a reason-then-judge process to direct reference-based comparison, thereby producing more accurate and reliable reward signals. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of both the Decomposed Graded Verifier trained with our Decoupled RL strategy and the pairwise verification paradigm.

blocks.en: In this section we prove that Decomposed Graded Verification preserves the true quality ordering of generated samples more faithfully than Discrete Binary Verification. The argument rests on a single observation: under GRPO, the relative update strength among samples is dictated by their group-normalized advantages, whose ordering is fully inherited from the underlying reward values. It therefore suffices to compare how the two reward designs rank pairs of samples with distinct latent quality.

blocks.en: By Lemma A.1 , GRPO assigns larger update weights to samples with larger rewards. Therefore, a reward model that better preserves the true quality ordering also provides more reliable relative policy updates. The decomposed graded reward is strictly monotonic with respect to the number of satisfied sub-questions and thus preserves all pairwise quality comparisons. In contrast, the binary reward collapses all imperfect samples into the same reward, making GRPO unable to distinguish partially correct samples from severely incorrect ones. Consequently, Decomposed Graded Verification provides a denser and more order-preserving reward signal for GRPO.
blocks.zh: 由Lemma A.1所出道,GRPO给样品分配了更大的更新权重,奖励更大. 因此,更好的保存真正质量订单的奖励模式也提供了更可靠的相对政策更新. 分解分级的奖励在满足子问题的数量上严格是单调的,从而保留了所有对等的质量比较. 相形之下,二进制奖励将所有不完美的样本倒塌为同一份奖励,使得GPRO无法将部分正确的样本与严重错误的样本区分开来. 因此,分级核查为GRPO提供了更密集、更能维持秩序的奖励信号。

By directly comparing generated outputs with ground-truth references, pairwise verification reduces reliance on internal target-state inference and can provide more reliable reward signals for policy optimization. These results further support the effectiveness of reference-based verification across different types of rule-governed visual generation tasks.

blocks.en: B.2 Sub-question-level Verification Accuracy
blocks.zh: B.2 次问题一级的核查准确性

blocks.en: The reliability of decomposed graded scoring depends on whether the verifier correctly judges individual sub-questions against the generated image. Even when the decomposition is appropriate, incorrect local judgments can introduce noise into the aggregated reward. We therefore directly evaluate sub-question-level verification accuracy on a held-out set of 200 binary sub-question samples. Three authors and two Ph.D. students each annotate 40 samples, collectively providing human labels for all 200 samples. We additionally obtain binary annotations from GPT-5.5 and Gemini-3.1-Pro on the same evaluation set. We compare the base model, the SFT-trained graded verifier, and the graded verifier further optimized with Decoupled RL, reporting accuracy against each annotation source separately.
blocks.zh: 分解分级分数的可靠性取决于核查者是否正确判断出单个子问题与生成的图像. 即使分解是适当的,不正确的局部判断也会将噪音带入汇总的奖励. 因此,我们直接评估一组200个二元分问题样本的分问题核查准确性。 3名作者和2名博士生每人对40个样本进行注释,集体为所有200个样本提供人类标签. 我们还从GPT-5.5和双子座3.1-Pro获得关于同一套评价的二进制说明。 我们比较了基础模型,SFT训练分级验证器,分级验证器与脱钩RL进一步优化,分别对照每个注释源报告准确性.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 5 , Decoupled RL substantially improves fine-grained verification accuracy across all three annotation sources. These results support the effectiveness of Decoupled RL in improving sub-question-level binary judgments and provide empirical evidence for the reliability of the local decisions underlying decomposed graded scoring.
blocks.zh: 如表5所示,脱钩RL大大改善了所有三个注释来源的精细校正准确性。 这些结果支持了脱钩RL在改进子问题级二进制判断方面的有效性,并为分解分级分级的当地决定的可靠性提供了经验证据.

blocks.en: B.3 Evaluation on Qwen-Image-2512
blocks.zh: B.3 对Quen-Image-2512的评价

blocks.en: To examine whether the effectiveness of our Decomposed Graded Verifier extends to a larger text-to-image generation backbone, we further evaluate Qwen-Image-2512 (20B), complementing the experiments on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium (2.5B) and FLUX.1-dev (12B). We compare the original model with its reinforcement learning variants guided by the Discrete Binary Verifier and the Decomposed Graded Verifier, respectively, using GenEval and CLIPScore for evaluation.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 6 , the Decomposed Graded Verifier improves the overall GenEval score from 0.74 to 0.82, outperforming the binary-reward counterpart by 0.06. The largest gains over the original model occur in attribute binding and position, which improve from 0.52 to 0.69 and from 0.38 to 0.51, respectively. These improvements suggest that fine-grained graded rewards are particularly useful for learning compositional requirements involving attribute associations and spatial relations. CLIPScore also increases from 34.1 to 35.3, compared with 34.4 under binary rewards. Together, these results extend the evidence for the effectiveness of decomposed graded rewards to a larger generation backbone with stronger baseline performance.

blocks.en: B.5 Sensitivity to the Number of Sub-questions
blocks.zh: B.5 对子问题数目的敏感性

blocks.en: To investigate how decomposition granularity affects global score estimation, we evaluate the trained Decomposed Graded Verifier on 200 held-out test samples. We explicitly instruct the verifier through the system prompt to generate sub-questions within three ranges: at most 10, 11–20, and 21–30. This experiment examines whether increasing the number of sub-questions consistently improves scoring accuracy or introduces additional errors through excessive decomposition.
blocks.zh: 为了调查分解颗粒性如何影响全球分数估计,我们评价200个停产测试样本上经过培训的分解分级验证器。 我们通过该系统明确指示核查人员在三个范围内产生子问题:最多10个、11-20个和21-30个。 这一实验研究的是,增加子问题的数量是否始终提高打分的准确性,还是通过过度分解引入了额外的错误.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 8 , the 11–20 setting achieves the lowest mean alignment error of 0.039, compared with 0.083 for at most 10 sub-questions and 0.072 for 21–30 sub-questions. These results suggest that an appropriate decomposition granularity improves scoring accuracy, while simply increasing the number of sub-questions does not guarantee better performance.
blocks.zh: 如表8所显示的,11至20个设置的平均对齐误差最低为0.039,而最多10个子问题为0.083个;21至30个子问题为0.072个。 这些结果表明,适当的分解颗粒性提高了打分的准确性,而仅仅增加子问题的数量并不能保证更好的性能.

blocks.en: Excessive decomposition can introduce redundant questions or requirements unsupported by the original prompt. For example, given “A red apple is placed on a table,” the verifier may repeatedly ask whether an apple exists or introduce questions such as “Is the apple a fruit?” and “Is the apple round?” that do not correspond to explicitly requested visual constraints. Such questions can distort the aggregated score by repeatedly weighting the same requirement or introducing irrelevant criteria. We also observe that generating more sub-questions can lead to violations of the required output format, reducing the reliability of the final score. Together, these observations highlight the importance of balancing fine-grained coverage with faithful and non-redundant decomposition.
blocks.zh: 过度分解可以引入由原始快取支持的冗余问题或要求. 例如,鉴于“一个红苹果被放在桌子上 ” , 核查者可能会反复询问苹果是否存在, 或引入诸如“苹果是水果吗?” 和“苹果圆?” 等与明确要求的视觉限制不符的问题。 这些问题会通过反复加权同一要求或引入不相干的标准来扭曲总分. 我们还认为,产生更多的子问题可能导致违反所要求的产出格式,降低最终分数的可靠性. 这些意见共同突出了在精细覆盖与忠实和非重复分解之间取得平衡的重要性。

blocks.en: Appendix C Limitations and Future Works
blocks.zh: 附录C 限制和未来工程

blocks.en: Our world-modeling evaluation is restricted to game-based environments with explicit rules, where the ground-truth image is uniquely determined by the initial task state and rule instructions. We adopt these controlled tasks primarily to evaluate the effectiveness of our pairwise verification paradigm. Although our results demonstrate the advantages of pairwise verification in these settings, these tasks capture only part of the complexity and diversity of real-world environments.
blocks.zh: 我们的世界建模评价仅限于有明确规则的基于游戏的环境,其中地面真实图像由初始任务状态和规则指令独有地来决定. 我们采取这些有控制的任务,主要是为了评估我们双向核查模式的有效性。 虽然我们的结果表明了在这些环境中对等核查的优势,但这些任务只抓住了现实世界环境的复杂性和多样性的一部分。

blocks.en: In future work, we plan to extend our investigation to open-ended settings with non-unique ground truths, construct larger and more realistic world-modeling datasets, and scale both the verifier and the generator to stronger backbones. Our long-term goal is to develop multimodal generative models that can reason about, simulate, and interact with complex real-world scenes.
blocks.zh: 在未来的工作中,我们计划扩大调查范围,将无限制的环境与非独特的地面真相联系起来,构建更大和更现实的世界模型化数据集,并将核查器和生成器扩大为更强大的骨干。 我们的长期目标是开发多种模式的遗传模型,这些模型能够对复杂的现实世界场景进行推理、模拟和互动。

blocks.en: Text-to-Image Verifier Prompt You are a powerful and trustworthy Text-to-Image Alignment Evaluator . Your responsibility is to evaluate the semantic alignment between a generated image and a text prompt. You must decompose the text prompt into verifiable atomic questions and score the consistency between the image and the prompt based strictly on visual evidence. Inputs You will be given the following inputs: • Text Prompt : the textual description used to generate the image. • Generated Image : the image produced by the text-to-image model. Evaluation Workflow Step 1: Prompt Decomposition Decompose the text prompt into a set of atomic questions that can be directly verified from the image. Each question must originate from facts explicitly stated in the text prompt and test one clear semantic assertion. Step 2: Image-Based Answering Answer each question solely based on the visual information present in the Generated Image. Do not introduce assumptions beyond the text prompt. Do not infer visual information that is absent, ambiguous, or cannot be confirmed from the image. Step 3: Consistency Judgement and Scoring For each question, determine whether the image-based answer is consistent with the information explicitly specified in the text prompt. If the image-based answer is consistent with the prompt, the question receives 1 point. Otherwise, it receives 0 points. Question Decomposition Principles The decomposed questions must satisfy the following requirements: • Each question must be binary, with a Yes or No answer. • Each question must be objectively verifiable through visual evidence. • Questions involving subjective judgment, emotions, aesthetics, or other non-verifiable properties are forbidden. • The number of questions should be naturally determined by the semantic complexity of the text prompt. The decomposition should follow the semantic order below when applicable: • Objects : existence, quantity, and category. • Object Attributes : color, shape, material, appearance, actions, and visible states. • Spatial Relations : relative position, orientation, and layout. • Non-Spatial Relations : interactions and action relations between entities. Output Requirements Output only a valid JSON object containing exactly two top-level fields: "sub_questions" and "final_score". Do not include Markdown code fences or additional text. { "sub_questions": [ { "id": 1, "question": "A decomposed sub-question", "answer": "True or False", "explanation": "Brief error explanation if False; otherwise an empty string" } ], "final_score": x } Replace the placeholders above with actual evaluation results. Include one entry for each distinct decomposed sub-question, with consecutive IDs starting at 1. Here, x = C / N \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{N} , where N \mathrm{N} is the total number of entries and C \mathrm{C} is the number answered "True". Output x \mathrm{x} as a JSON number rounded to two decimal places. Inputs for This Evaluation Text Prompt: $ { prompt } The attached image is the Generated Image. <image>

blocks.en: Rule-Governed World Modeling Verifier Prompt-Pairwise You are a powerful and trustworthy Image Editing Evaluator . Your responsibility is to evaluate whether an image editing model successfully completes a game-based image editing task according to the provided rules. Inputs You will be given the following inputs: • Initial Image : the original game state given to the image editing model. • Generated Image : the output produced by the image editing model. • Reference Image : the ground-truth result that correctly follows all rules. • Game Rules : the rules governing the game and editing constraints. Evaluation Workflow Step 1: Rule Decomposition Independently decompose the Game Rules into atomic, visually checkable rules, even if they are already decomposed. The resulting rules must remain consistent with the provided Game Rules. Step 2: Rule Violation Checking Use the Reference Image as the correct standard. Compare the Generated Image with the Reference Image rule by rule, and determine whether each rule is violated. Step 3: Scoring Let the total number of decomposed atomic rules be N \mathrm{N} , and let the number of violated rules be V \mathrm{V} . The score of the Generated Image is: Score = N − V N . \textnormal{Score}=\frac{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{N}}. The final score should reflect how consistently the Generated Image follows the rules compared with the Reference Image. Output Requirements Output only a valid JSON object with exactly two top-level fields: "sub_questions" and "final_score". Do not include Markdown code fences or additional text. { "sub_questions": [ { "id": 1, "question": "A decomposed rule sub-question", "answer": "True or False", "explanation": "Brief rule-violation explanation if False; otherwise an empty string" } ], "final_score": x } Replace the placeholders above with actual evaluation results. Include one entry for each distinct decomposed atomic rule, with consecutive IDs starting at 1. Here, x \mathrm{x} is the score calculated in Step 3, expressed as a JSON number rounded to two decimal places. Inputs for This Evaluation Game Rules: $ { game_rules } Images are attached in this order: Initial Image, Generated Image, Reference Image. <image><image><image>
